title: Oct 7 Results + Oct 8 Preview: When the Model Keeps the Faith
summary: A 1-3 showing on Oct 7, but here's why tomorrow's White Sox pick tells a different story

content.value:
## Here's the Thing About Tough Days

Look, I'm not going to sugarcoat it—October 7th was rough. A 1-3 record isn't what anyone wants to wake up to, and that 25% accuracy stings a little. But you know what's interesting? Sometimes the story behind the numbers matters more than the numbers themselves.

## The Full Picture

The Dodgers came through for us—our only win of the day at 51% confidence. But the Yankees, Padres, and White Sox? Not so much. What's worth noting is how close these probabilities were. We're talking 50-54% range across the board. These weren't slam dunks; they were coin flips with slightly better odds.

## Tomorrow's Story: Round Two in Chicago

And here's where it gets interesting. The model is sending us right back to the same matchup that opened our day yesterday—Guardians at White Sox. Only this time, we've got different arms on the mound.

Parker Messick takes the ball for Cleveland, while Hagen Smith gets the nod for Chicago. The White Sox are sitting at that same 50% confidence level, which means the model sees this as a true toss-up with the slightest edge to the home team.

content.title: ⭐ Tomorrow's Top Pick - October 8
content.sub: 50% win probability · Smith vs Messick · Guardians @ White Sox

content.value:
## Why I'm Not Worried

Here's the human angle: baseball doesn't owe us anything. A 50% probability means exactly that—it could go either way. The fact that three of our four picks yesterday landed in that razor-thin margin tells me the model is being honest about uncertainty rather than forcing confidence where it doesn't exist.

That Dodgers win? That was our second-lowest confidence pick, and it hit. Sometimes the 51-percenters come through while the 54-percenters don't. That's October baseball.

So tomorrow, we go back to Chicago. Same teams, different pitchers, same 50-50 odds. And honestly? I kind of love that the model isn't backing down.
